items.title: Federal securities or derivatives-market authority
kv: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission · Commodity Futures Trading Commission
A legally classified securities-market or derivatives-market activity calls for the applicable SEC or CFTC registration, designation, supervision, or rule route.
Federal securities laws and the Commodity Exchange Act, each within its statutory perimeter.

Classify the instrument, contract, and activity. · Identify the exact entity and applicable SEC, CFTC, or SRO route. · Recover current registration, designation, order, exemption, rulebook, and effective-date evidence.

U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission · Commodity Futures Trading Commission · SEC or CFTC offices acting under delegated authority · Self-regulatory organizations only within their separate statutory rulemaking roles
Neither tokenization nor a technical ledger decides securities/commodity classification or creates SEC/CFTC permission.

items.title: Federal bank chartering, supervision, and deposit-insurance route
kv: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency · Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System · Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation
A U.S. banking activity requires a charter, supervision, deposit-insurance analysis, or a related federal banking permission.
Applicable National Bank Act, Federal Reserve, and Federal Deposit Insurance Act authorities.

Federal supervision, a bank affiliation, preliminary charter approval, or deposit insurance does not establish a particular product authority, bank account, or affiliate permission.

items.title: Entity governing documents and formation-law route
kv: The question is who may direct a legal entity, appoint officers, authorize contracts, or allocate internal fiduciary and voting powers.
Applicable entity-formation law plus charter, bylaws/operating agreement, board or member action, and contract; Delaware corporate law is the bounded statutory example.

Identify the exact legal entity and formation jurisdiction. · Recover current governing documents and the relevant authorization record. · Separate entity governance from regulatory permission, network governance, and asset-holder rights.

Boards of directors of corporations · Managers of manager-managed LLCs · Members of member-managed LLCs · Other entity governing bodies only as provided by applicable formation law and governing documents
A corporate board, foundation, DAO vote, or product committee does not obtain public-law authority or control a separately issued asset absent the governing instrument and applicable law.

items.title: SRO rulebook governance subject to SEC process
kv: The Depository Trust Company · National Securities Clearing Corporation · Fixed Income Clearing Corporation
A securities SRO's participant, membership, trading, clearing, or disciplinary rule is the claimed source of governance.
Exchange Act section 19 proposed-rule process plus the SRO's effective rulebook.

Identify the SRO and exact rule version. · Confirm the rule's Commission filing/approval or effectiveness status as applicable. · Establish that the entity, participant, instrument, and event are within the rule's scope.
National securities exchanges acting as SROs · Registered securities associations · Registered clearing agencies with applicable SRO rule obligations
An SRO's private operating rulebook is not a general federal statute, and a corporate or protocol rulebook is not an SRO rulebook merely because market participants use it.
